subject: Island 014 threejs chroma-projected sculpted honey cathedral relief first gate

inputs.evidenceIntegrity: All seven required r02 materials-on/off PNG hashes match screenshot-manifest.v2.json. The manifest explicitly excludes failed WebGL loading-screen attempts, and no excluded image was scored.

perViewScores.note: The generated front is rich and door-led, but it redesigns the exact source into a taller, denser multi-dome cathedral. Host geometry remains visible behind the cutout, and a cyan/teal fringe traces the projected silhouette.
The actual naked relief is a full-height rectangular triangulated sheet. No palace silhouette, doorway hierarchy, bay bodies, or meaningful sculpted depth exists in the geometry.

The palace artwork shears as one near-planar image. A long vertical paper edge and unsupported lower edge float ahead of the sealed host, while a cyan fringe outlines domes and finials. Apparent honeycomb bays are texture cells rather than four attached three-dimensional bay bodies.
The oblique wireframe exposes a single broad rectangular mesh wall with negligible local depth, a hard paper edge, and a large gap/overhang relative to the host.
The opposite oblique repeats the same flat-card, detached-edge, and cyan-fringe defects. The textured front does not hand off to or integrate with the solid host.
The opposite naked view independently confirms the same rectangular sheet, negligible relief, hard paper edge, and floating relationship to the host.

The projected texture has excellent close-range royal-door and honey ornament readability, but this is baked image detail; the materials-off and oblique evidence prove it is not carried by coherent attached relief geometry.

exactEvidence: oblique-045-materials-on: full projected palace shears as one plane with a hard left/right edge
oblique-315-materials-on: same hard edge and planar artwork from the opposite side
oblique-045-materials-off and oblique-315-materials-off: full rectangular triangulated sheet is directly visible

cyanBackgroundOrFringe.exactEvidence: A bright cyan/teal one-to-several-pixel fringe traces external domes, finials, lower drips, and side contours in front, 45, and 315 materials-on captures.

detachedOrFloatingProjection.exactEvidence: Both materials-on obliques show unsupported lower and vertical cutout edges floating ahead of the sealed host; both materials-off obliques expose the same gap and overhang.

invalidEvidence.exactEvidence: Every scored PNG matches screenshot-manifest.v2.json. The unavailable WebGL loading-screen attempts are explicitly excluded and absent from the scored set.

projectionDominatesRearOrBackwards.exactEvidence: No rear capture was supplied at this first gate; the family already fails on required front and oblique evidence.

doorNotFirstRoseNotSecond.exactEvidence: Within the materials-on artwork, the large purple bee doorway is first and the smaller rose/window region is secondary in front and both obliques.

fewerThanFourAttachedCountableBays.exactEvidence: The materials-on obliques show many baked honey cells, but the intended four attached bay bodies are not independently countable; materials-off reveals no bay relief at all, only the rectangular grid.

largestMismatch: The exact source is a compact inhabited three-dimensional honey cathedral with deep attached bays and layered civic mass. This family is a high-quality generated front image placed on a full rectangular triangulated sheet; it shears like a billboard, floats ahead of the accepted host, and carries cyan fringe around its cutout edges.

gateEvaluation.finding: Although the textured front has strong phone-scale decoration and a correct door-first hierarchy, the actual geometry fails the naked gate at 0.08 and triggers billboard/paper-edge, cyan-fringe, detached-projection, and missing-attached-bay hard vetoes. Under the Gauntlet, a first-pass hard veto or critical score below 0.50 retires the construction family immediately; the unused correction allowance cannot be spent on this family.
